correctness.rationale: For all odd primes, the norm-one conic has cyclic size N=p−χ(−1) and the Fourier self-restriction is multiplicative convolution. An unramified character DFT diagonalizes it integrally. For every character degree r, character orthogonality annihilates all binomial residues below k=min(r,N−r); at k the residue is N/(2^k k!), doubled only at r=N/2, hence a unit. Earlier coefficients divisible by p have π-adic order at least p−1+j>k; they cannot cancel. Thus the exact local Smith exponents are 0,1,1,...,m, their sum is m² and no eigenvalue vanishes. The included checker confirms predicted modular ranks for primes 3,5,7,11,13,17 at all characteristic-p-valid truncation lengths. Its p=3 truncation cannot by itself resolve the final exponent, which the proof resolves. An independent exact cyclotomic determinant expansion for the prime 3 also returns 9, verifying the aggregate determinant valuation at the only boundary where the truncated characteristic-p model cannot see the largest exponent.

value.rationale: Exact arithmetic conditioning of the natural self-conic finite Fourier transform is a motivated invariant in finite-field Heisenberg uniqueness and reconstruction. The result covers an unbounded prime family of both split and nonsplit norm-one conics, proves invertibility and computes each local elementary divisor, not merely an isolated nonzero minor or routine renaming. It makes no unverified claim about Archimedean singular numbers or extension-field generalization.
